project: defender — an LLM SOC-analyst agent (python, pytest, uv)

gate.test: cd defender && flock /tmp/defender-pytest.lock uv run pytest tests/ -m "not live and not gate" -n auto --dist loadfile --ignore tests/e2e/test_540_box_boundary.py
checks: the baseline-ratcheted custom lints under scripts/lint/lint_*.py (monkeypatch, unsafe-jsonl-io, raw-git-subprocess, unanchored-default, vulture, duplicate-helpers, …) — each blocks only on a NEW finding, and each documents an inline-suppression escape hatch in its own module
gate.notes: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the source of truth — run what it runs; don't trust this list to stay current. Running in a git worktree? The shared `.venv` editable install points at the main checkout — prepend `PYTHONPATH=<worktree-root>` to the pytest call or you test the wrong tree. EVERY pytest invocation on this box goes through one lock — prefix it `flock /tmp/defender-pytest.lock`, ad-hoc subsets and adversary runs included, not just the command above. Two sessions launching fleets independently put 20 xdist workers on 12 cores and OOM-killed the container; the lock makes them take the box in turn instead of thrashing it. It costs nothing when nothing else is running. `test` above is CI's full-suite command, recorded so you can read what CI runs — a spec-flow leaf never runs it; it runs its own suite's files.

tests.harness: defender/tests/e2e/_replay_harness.py — a new scenario is a few lines of `Turn(...)`, not fresh plumbing. Build on it rather than inventing parallel machinery.
tests.idioms: Fakes enter through the entry point's injection seams (a `deps` parameter, a constructor argument), never `monkeypatch.setattr` — CI ratchets new setattr sites (`scripts/lint/lint_monkeypatch.py`).

ticket_store.note: #767 renamed the writer's second call from close_case_ticket (a POST /tickets/{key}/transitions close) to record_case_ticket (a POST /tickets/{key}/comments record) — the host now records its investigation as a comment and never transitions the case; a person CLOSES it, and that close is what releases the case's comments to a later run's gather (the read side keys on `status`, never on a label or a comment's author). The writer's egress still bypasses guard_outbound entirely (it calls transport.docker_exec_curl directly, never confine_read_endpoint), so it is staged nowhere a `staged`-style record would see it (F3). Three test implementors of the duck-typed `ticket_writer=` seam moved with the rename: defender/tests/_spec791.py::SpecTail, defender/tests/test_947_triplet_sibling.py's inline Writer, and the #767 spec's own defender/tests/test_767_run_tail.py::Tail (g10).

learning_queue.note: ADDED BY #921's GROUNDING: `evals/harness.py::materialize` is a writer of this sink's shape that no import-following census sees — it `shutil.copy`s a scenario's own findings.jsonl into `<tmp>/defender/learning/_pending/findings.jsonl` and copytrees a `runs/` fixture beside it, then runs the real author against that tree. It is a HARNESS edge, not a loop edge, and it is the reason a row-shape change has a second consumer. Also worth pinning for the next census: the findings channel has ONE gate (`CorpusAuthorConfig.gate`, wired to `learning/author/lessons/run.py::_gate_findings`), called once per tick over EVERY keyed row of findings.jsonl — so two directions in one file share one gate and one batch, and the gate indexes entry['finding_id'|'run_id'|'direction'] directly inside drain's stuck-recording guard, where a missing key takes the whole tick's batch to `<channel>.stuck.jsonl`. UPDATED BY #922: `QUEUEABLE_FINDING_TYPES` is now the ONLY finding-`type` vocabulary left, and `learning/judge/enqueue.py::_validate_row` is its one production consumer. The set it used to be shadowed by — the pipeline judge's document validator in `core/validate.py` — was deleted with that judge.

run_dir.note: Four writers were added after #771's phase-F reconciliation found the same hole in three instruments at once. The driver's fault-exit trace write (`write_text("")` onto the fixed tool_trace.jsonl name observe.write_trace also owns) is one of the two sites that issue reported and was missing from the test census, the write lint's gate list AND this list. The queries-table append is the query tool's SECOND artifact — the payload write was censused, the table was not. The lead-claim hook and the atomic helper are the two the original grep could not see. EVERY ENTRY MUST NAME A SYMBOL THAT RESOLVES: three of the four added here did not (a leading underscore the driver's entry point does not have, an actor id where the code symbol was `_revert_strays`, and a render-lane function renamed at some point), and a resolver following a name that resolves to nothing gets the same answer as one following a row that was never written. This list seeds the next run's census, so a gap here becomes a gap in every downstream instrument. `scrub` stays under readers deliberately: #771's scan verdict is written OUTSIDE the tree it judges (§7 D8), so the walk remains a pure reader of the run dir and the marker belongs to no run-dir writer census. ADDED BY #992's GROUNDING: three writers the list never carried although #796/#923 built them — `close_tool._commit` (report.md, write_guarded mode=replace, the ONLY writer of that file), `challenge_gate.write_review_record` (review_record.{turn}.json, keyed on ReviewState.turns+1 at the committing arms and on turns at the challenged arm) and `challenge_gate._write_trace_row` (wire_logs/review_{role}_trace.jsonl, guarded append, one file per REVIEW_ROLES member). #992 puts `inconclusive` through the gate, so all three now fire on the disposition that used to write only the first two; the readers added are the run-page consumers that split reviewed from unreviewed attempts — `visualize_runtime._was_reviewed` reads that split OFF THE RECORD — `_commit` writes `reviewed: true` on the reviewed site and `false` on the `unresolved` bypass (#992, settled at the merge gate after two inferences broke: keying on the `NO_REVIEW_DISPOSITIONS` constant re-rendered pre-#992 bypasses as reviewed once the set shrank; keying on surviving trace rows rendered any run dir whose traces were relocated or pruned as a bypass). A record with no `reviewed` field is read by the bypass set of its day, frozen in the visualizer. ADDED BY #773's GROUNDING (base 3b4f5797): `verify_forward/engine.py::_run_verify_pydantic` is a WRITER of this root and no census ever listed it. The forward check's verifier stage binds `StageContext(learning_run_dir=source_run_dir)` where `source_run_dir = ctx.runs_dir / ctx.source_id` (checks.py:87, engine.py:66), and `_pydantic_stage.run_stage` then writes the whole wire stream to `<run_dir>/wire_logs/<trace_name>` via `observe.stage_trace_path` — with `trace_name = f"{prefix}.{stem}.{check_index}.trace.jsonl"` composed at checks.py:59. episode_dir.note: Declared by #947's grounding. AT b8a63e66 `capture.py:130-136` composes it as `resolve_runs_base()/'episodes'/<id>/` — a sibling of the run dirs, inside the runs base. #947 MOVES BOTH ENDS OF THAT, and this note is written against the design, not the base: (1) the episodes root becomes a CONFIGURED location (`DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE`), outside both the runs base and the checkout, with NO default derivation — a reader that re-derives it from the runs base silently restores the containment hole the relocation closed (#947 §7 round 2, F5-EPISODE-ROOT); and (2) the three sibling run dirs move UNDER it, at `{episode_dir}/runs/`, so the episode dir is a PARENT of run dirs rather than their sibling. `cli.py::episode_dir_for` is the symbol whose semantics change: it is the production resolver every reader of an episode must go through once the root is configured, and the one to follow instead of re-composing a path. The old safety clause here read 'a SIBLING of the run dirs, never inside one, so it is not bound into any box' — that is verbatim the reason `capture.py:134`'s waiver states, and #947 REFUTES it on that reason (claim C26): the episode dir now contains three rw box binds. The conclusion survives on a different ground, recorded as an examined no: the bind is the run dir alone, `served/` and `worlds/` stay unreachable from inside a box, and every archive read goes through the `_layout.artifact_file` / `stage_tables` screens. Rewrite `capture.py:134`'s waiver text in the same commit that moves the root. Today it holds only `served/`: `prime_base` writes `served/base.jsonl` once and `Ledger.record` appends `served/<world_id>.jsonl`, one writer per file — which is the whole of the launcher's parallel-safety premise. The directory is created as a side effect of `_io.append_jsonl`'s parent mkdir, NOT through `guarded_mkdir`, and NOTHING anywhere removes an episode dir: both `prepare_episode` and `prime_base` treat an existing one as a permanent refusal. #947 adds family.yaml, staged.yaml, review.yaml, provenance.json, worlds/<X>/ AND runs/<sibling>/ here — add those writers (staging.py, review.py, archive.py, _family.py) IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATES THEM, not before: a row naming a symbol that resolves to nothing is indistinguishable to a resolver from a row nobody wrote. ADDED IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATED THEM, as the sentence above requires: `write_family` (family.yaml), `record_staged` and `_record_teardown_failure` (staged.yaml and the teardown block of review.yaml), `review` (review.yaml), `archive_episode` (worlds/<X>/), and `cli._record_episode_outcome` / `_write_family_stamp` (the episode's own outcome and its provenance.json). The readers gain the two derived readers, the staging record's own reader and the manifest loader. ADDED BY #921's GROUNDING (re-verified at base 9f4e8247, where #947's relocation HAS landed: `episodes_root()` is $DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE with no default derivation, refused inside the runs base and inside REPO_ROOT, and the sibling run dirs live at {episode_dir}/runs/ via the episode layout's own runs segment — `_episode_paths.RUNS_DIRNAME`, reached as `EpisodePaths(...).runs`; at that base it was a constant on cli.py, then on archive.py, and #1077 D7 moved it to the owner). The writer this list was missing is `observe.RequestLogger`: `learning/branch/seams.py::model_seam` builds StageContext(learning_run_dir=episode_dir), and `_pydantic_stage.run_stage` writes every questioner and comparator call's FULL wire stream to `<episode_dir>/wire_logs/<agent_id>_trace.jsonl` through `observe.stage_trace_path` (guarded_mkdir) + `open_guarded` — the seam's own docstring says 'THE TRACE LANDS IN THE EPISODE'. #921's per-world judge calls multiply that stream by worlds x draws and each one carries the whole 10-32K-token prompt verbatim, so a census that lists only judge.yaml and worlds/<X>/judge/ under-counts the writers by the largest artifact in the tree. `_archived_labels` is added beside `verdicts`/`delta_o` because it is the reader that turns `worlds/` into the label set both of them iterate. STILL TRUE and worth keeping: NOTHING removes an episode dir, and `capture.py:134`'s lint-unguarded-tree-write waiver STILL reads 'the episode archive is `runs_base/episodes/<id>/`, a sibling of the run dirs' — refuted text that the commit moving the root was supposed to rewrite and did not. ADDED BY #1049's GROUNDING (base 085b76e0): the RECORD readers this census never listed — every sentence-formatting reader of the episode tree that #1049 rewrites onto the root-bound primitive (`_io.bind(root)` → `.read(name)` / `.read_jsonl(name)` / `.under(name)`, the shape resolved at #1049's §7) (family's YAML screen and its review/samples/manifest/report/ledger/archived-text readers, `_missing_required_input`'s lstat gate, `lead_chain`'s gather-summary read, the grade record's two readers, the stamp/staged/timing readers, `branch/episode.py`'s eval-lane outcome read, and the page's `load_episode`) — plus three writers of records INTO the episode dir that were missing: `_write_judge_yaml` (judge.yaml, the record `ungradable_reason` and `not_graded.reason` land in), `_write_wire_log` (the judge's framed prompt copies), and `staging.merge_review` (the ONE merger of review.yaml, which `cli._record_episode_outcome` and `_record_teardown_failure` both go through — `cli.py:1055` records an `ArchiveRefused` sentence naming `<episode_dir>/runs/...` or `<episode_dir>/worlds/...` into `episode.reason` there). `read_record` itself is deliberately NOT listed: it does not exist until write-code-from-spec builds it — add `_io.py::bind` (and the bound reader's `read` / `read_jsonl` / `under`) here in the commit that creates them.

elastic_corpus.note: Declared by #947's grounding as an EMPTY-WRITER root, which is the fact worth recording: at b8a63e66 nothing in defender/ creates an Elasticsearch index or alias (re-verified: the only `_aliases`/`put_alias` hits are a yaml dumper flag and the model-provider alias table). Every listed reader reaches the cluster through the one read-confined door, `elastic_adapter._http_json` -> `confinement.guard_outbound` -> `confine_read_endpoint(verb_class='r')`, whose elastic allowlist is exactly `/*/_search POST`, `/_query POST`, `/_cluster/health GET`, `/api/status GET`. #947's corpus staging is the FIRST writer; it must call `transport.docker_exec_curl` directly, and note that `guard_outbound` is also the capture recorder, so a write door that skips it records nothing anywhere but `staged.yaml`. #947 LANDS THAT FIRST WRITER and this row now names it: `staging._Door` reaches `docker_exec_curl` directly with PUT/POST/DELETE, outside `guard_outbound`, so `staged.yaml` is the only record any of these writes happened. The host-side reads are listed beside them because `_count` and `_resolve/index` are deliberately absent from the adapter's read allowlist — they exist only on this door.

box_env.note: DECLARED BY #1092's GROUNDING (base b016749c). The environment a granted program runs under inside a box: `BOX_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (runtime/box_codec.py, MOVED THERE BY #1096 from box/_spec.py, which now re-exports it along with `_BOX_MARK_ENV` — the owner is the stdlib module the in-box entrypoint imports, so the entrypoint's per-exec closure does not pay for the `box` package door) is the ONE key set, rendered onto `docker run --env` by BOTH argv builders (`_create_argv` indexes `env_pairs[key]` for every allowlist key with NO default — a key added to the allowlist and not to `infra_env`/`_LOCALE_ENV` is a KeyError on every two-arg start; `_render_env` merges locale defaults, then the caller's allowlisted keys VALUE-BLIND, then the derived infra keys which win), inherited by every `docker exec`, and re-filtered from `os.environ` by the entrypoint (`bash_exec.py::_run_box_entrypoint`) before any command runs. The two HOST lanes are writers of the same shape and are listed because the allowlist governs them too: `_host_fallback_env` copies every allowlisted key out of `request.env` and `run_env` inherits the operator's whole `os.environ` — so a key that joins the allowlist reaches the unsandboxed lane through those two copies whenever the caller or the shell carries it. The READERS the static walk cannot see are the three granted shell shims (`bin/defender-sql:9-10`, `bin/defender-invlang:7-8`, `bin/defender-lessons:8-9`; `bin/defender-policy:9-10` ungranted) — each `exec`s `${DEFENDER_DIR}/.venv/bin/python3` when it is executable, else bare `python3` — and `scripts/_venv.py::reexec_into_venv`, which `os.execv`s into `defender/.venv/bin/python3` when that path `is_file()`; both are cross-process edges classified by hand in #1092's brief.

tenant_root.note: DECLARED BY #1078's GROUNDING (base ed5386bc) as an EMPTY-WRITER root, which is the fact worth recording: at this base nothing in defender/ or scripts/ writes or reads a data root or a tenant row — `grep -rn 'tenant\.json' --include=*.py defender scripts` (no tests) finds only `_tenant.py`'s docstrings and `TENANT_RECORD_NAME = '_tenant.json'`, the RUNS-BASE record, which is a different file under a different root (`runs_base`). #1078 makes `<data root>/<tenant>/` (DEFENDER_DATA_ROOT, REQUIRED: there is no code default, and an unset or empty value is refused naming the variable, per #1078 §7 J01) the PARENT of four roots already declared here: `runs/` (was runs_base), `sessions/` (session_store, derived as runs_base.parent/sessions and unchanged), `episodes/` (was episode_dir's DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE) and `learning/` (was learning_queue / pending_dir / learning_run_dir's state root, plus the three drain/repo locks drain_worktree's writers take). Its own record is the tenant ROW `<root>/<T>/tenant.json`, whose ONE production writer is to be `_tenant.py::create_tenant` (write_guarded mode=create) and whose readers are to be `require_tenant` and `tenant_of_run_dir`. NONE OF THOSE SYMBOLS EXISTS YET — add each here in the commit that creates it, per this block's rule that a row naming a symbol that resolves to nothing is indistinguishable from a row nobody wrote. `_tenant.py` is in lint_unguarded_tree_write's LINT_HARD_GATED_MODULES, so the tenant folder's own mkdir must be `guarded_mkdir`, and every new module-level str constant in `_tenant.py` is an import-refused 'record name' under lint_run_records arm (c) unless it joins `_OWNER_NON_RECORD_EXPORTS`. When #1078 lands, the six rows its C45 names (runs_base, episode_dir, learning_queue, pending_dir, learning_run_dir, session_store) go stale on their knob names and resolver symbols (`resolve_runs_base`, `DEFENDER_RUNS_BASE`, `DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE`, `DEFAULT_PATHS`) — rewrite them in that commit. RE-VERIFIED BY #1120's GROUNDING (base a1c65801): #1078 pass (A) has landed, so the 'NONE OF THOSE SYMBOLS EXISTS YET' sentence above is STALE — `spec-graph trace resource tenant_root` resolves the writer `create_tenant` (its one production call, scripts/tenant.py:54, inside `setup`) and the readers `require_tenant` (run_common.py:88, scripts/tenant.py:52) and `tenant_of_run_dir` (run.py:359, learning/branch/cli.py:346); `resolve_data_root` has exactly six production call sites (_tenant.py:384,390,402; run_common.py:86; learning/branch/cli.py:1046; scripts/tenant.py:49). #1120 (D1/D2) adds `<T>/knowledge/` (the tenant's settings/ + agent/ halves: an operator-placed git clone or plain folder that `setup` ADOPTS without writing into it — DC2, rewritten here under §7-verify V6) UNDER this root — declared separately as `tenant_knowledge`; there is NO `<T>/.knowledge.partial` (DC2 withdrew setup's staging), the one-tenant guard's row-less inner scan admits exactly the name `knowledge` (MF1), and setup's one write stays the row through `create_tenant`, after the folder rules pass (rules-first) — and absorbs `TenantPaths` into a `Tenant` built only by `accept_tenant`. `TenantPaths(` is constructed at 7 production sites today (_tenant.py:282,338,390,403; run_common.py:94; learning/branch/cli.py:1046; scripts/tenant.py:51) and named by 16 demands of spec_graph_1078-pass-a.yaml; rewrite this row and those in the commit that removes it. LANDED BY #1120 piece 1: the public `TenantPaths` is gone. Its constructor and its J03/O11a guards survive as the PRIVATE `_tenant._TenantPaths` (M4), constructed only inside `_tenant.py` (accept_tenant, accept_placed_knowledge, create_tenant, require_tenant, tenant_of_run_dir); `Tenant`'s paths are pure joins through `_TenantLayout`, the unguarded layout `_TenantPaths` extends. conventions.dangerLens: adversarial input — alert data is attacker-influenced by definition, and malicious input is well-formed on purpose. Use this as write-tests' fourth enumeration lens unless the change's danger zone is clearly elsewhere (environment/resource, or concurrency when the design admits parallel invocation).

codeGraph.notes: defender is a namespace package (no defender/__init__.py; pyproject at defender/, not the repo root), so pyrefly's import root defaults to defender/ and `defender.x` imports silently resolve to Unknown. searchPath is relative to configDir: `..` = repo root (makes `defender` a top-level package, mirroring pytest's pythonpath=['..']), `.` = defender/.
